categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Cases where the fine is created and promptly paid with little to no intervening notification or penalty steps, resulting in very short durations and straightforward fulfillment.
categories.rationale: High frequency variants like V0002 and V0007 clearly group here as they skip complex notifications or appeals and go straight to payment.

categories.name: Standard Collection / Escalation
categories.description: Standard processing involving fine creation, fine notifications, penalties, and eventual escalation to credit collection after extended periods of non-payment.
categories.rationale: Dominates the high-frequency baseline (e.g., V0001, V0004) where notifications and penalties are standard before terminating in credit collection or delayed payment.

categories.name: Payment Rework Loop
categories.description: Cases characterized by multiple repeated payment attempts or fragmented installments over a prolonged trace length and duration.
categories.rationale: Variants V0005, V0006, and long tail cases like V0153, V0151 display repeated payment activities constituting an installment-like or corrective payment pattern.

categories.name: Appeal and Prefecture Handling
categories.description: Complex lifecycle paths that involve formal appeals to the prefecture or judge, results notifications, and deeply extended durations spanning multiple years.
categories.rationale: Characterized by activities such as Insert Date Appeal to Prefecture, Send Appeal to Prefecture, and Receive Result Appeal from Prefecture (e.g., V0008, V0057, V0103).
